stem: Nitin starts at point P facing South. He walks 5 m South, then turns right and walks 12 m. He then turns right again and walks 5 m. What is the straight-line distance from P to Nitin's current position?

per_option_rationale.rationale: South 5 m, right turn to West, West 12 m, right turn to North, North 5 m. The two 5 m legs cancel. Net displacement = 12 m West from P.
Student adds all three leg lengths (5+12+5=22) to get the path length, not the straight-line distance from P.
Student ignores the third 5 m leg and treats the endpoint as (12 m West, 5 m South), giving sqrt(144+25)=13 via the 5-12-13 triple.
Student adds only the first and second leg lengths (5+12=17), treating the path as a straight two-leg sum without any geometry.

explanation: Starting at P facing South: walk 5 m to (0,-5). Turn right (now West): walk 12 m to (-12,-5). Turn right (now North): walk 5 m to (-12,0). The North and South legs cancel (5 m South then 5 m North). The net position is 12 m due West of P. Distance = 12 m.

explanation_sections.punchline: The answer is 12 m. Two right turns from South give West then North, and the two 5 m vertical legs cancel perfectly, leaving only the 12 m horizontal displacement.
explanation_sections.approach: Plot each leg as a vector. Assign coordinates: right = positive x, up = positive y. Sum the x components and y components separately. Final distance = sqrt(x^2 + y^2). Check for cancellation before computing.
explanation_sections.lesson: Legs on the same axis but in opposite directions cancel. Always sum displacement vectors, not path lengths. The 5-12-13 trap appears if any leg is ignored.
explanation_sections.timing: 120 seconds. Tracking three direction changes takes about 40 seconds. Checking cancellation takes 20 seconds. Computing sqrt(144+0) takes under 10 seconds. Reserve remaining time to verify the turn directions.
